disclosures.name: TestAllThreadsSyscallSignals
disclosures.reason: CLASS NOTE (coordinator ruling 2026-09-03, mailbox 82ec6654c): this entry carries `cgo-configuration`, the class syscall's three sibling entries carry, and it DOES NOT FIRE YET -- measured before it was minted: matchTerminalStatuses unlocks a Go=pass / C#=skip pair for `platform-skip` alone (its own comment says no other class unlocks the shape) and sends every other class to the generic arm, which requires C#=fail, so the class could never fire. The ruling is to make the PIPELINE admit the class rather than re-label the entries, because the class name carries WHY (the cgo axis, ruled the state of record the same day) and re-labelling would throw that away; the admitting arm, its positive control and syscall's missing TestUseCgroupFD entry land in their own converter seat, and this row validates at its re-annotated `linux: 28 + 2` only once that seat lands. Both are train 22, so the landed master carries them together. The rest: the converted corpus is behaviourally a cgo-LINKED Go build for this seam, and the oracle is pinned cgo-OFF (the state of record on every platform since 2026-09-03), so this verdict is the residue of that mismatch, not a capability gap. Measured at the pinned state (go1.23.12 linux/amd64, Release, tiering off, the 2026-09-03 Linux leveling re-sweep at 22d2bd9dc): Go=pass, C#=skip. Go passes because at CGO_ENABLED=0 its runtime really does stop the world and replay the syscall on every thread; the converted side skips because runtime_doAllThreadsSyscall answers ENOTSUP -- the answer a cgo-linked Go build gives, which is why this very test opens by skipping on it with the message pinned as this entry's signature. The row's Linux line was banked (29 + 2) under the Linux host's default cgo-ON, where Go skipped too and the pair matched by a coincidence of errno; under the pinned state the honest shape is this disclosure, never a match.

disclosures.name: TestSignalTrace
disclosures.signature: the go2cs managed runtime has no execution tracer
disclosures.reason: the test wraps its signal exercise in runtime/trace.Start, and Go's execution tracer is a serialization of the scheduler the managed host does not have: StartTrace stops the world through the g/m/p machinery (semacquire's first step is getg, a per-thread runtime structure with no CLR counterpart). runtime.StartTrace returns an error by signature, so the linux hand-own answers a named tracing-not-supported error — the AllThreadsSyscall→ENOTSUP fidelity pattern — and the test fails cleanly asserting trace output it cannot have. The signal delivery under the trace is the part this row's siblings already prove; the tracer itself is the same class of unimplementable runtime machinery as WriteHeapDump. LINUX RETIRED 2026-09-27 (Q28, the managed execution tracer): runtime.StartTrace now succeeds on linux and windows through golib's ExecutionTracer, and TestSignalTrace passes on linux (os/signal linux 29 + 1). Darwin keeps this entry: its StartTrace is still the converted body, no darwin tracer exists, and no fleet host measures darwin
